svg.text: No finite change of the primes is a sumset A + B with |A|, |B| >= 2
A. A two-element summand covers a vanishing share
Share of primes p <= N with p - d or p + d prime
B. Residues mod 13 split into two sides
S = A mod 13, T = B mod 13, S + T = all nonzero residues
A: exact sieve counts to 10^8, cross-checked by trial division at 10^5. For d = 2 the count 880,623 is 2 x 440,312 - 1, twice the
known twin-prime pair count. Each curve eventually falls like c_d / log N (large d only starts falling later), so A must be infinite.
B: all 484,094 admissible pairs mod 13. T avoids -S, so |S| + |T| <= 13 and one side uses at most 6 of 13 classes, at every
prime at once; this squeezes A and B to about sqrt(x) elements up to x. Finite data illustrate the obstruction; they prove nothing.
